title: Sahih Muslim
author: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi
edition_analyzed: Standard Arabic edition with contemporary English translations
target_audience: Non-Muslims interested in Islamic primary sources
core_themes: Teachings and sayings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
Faith, practice, and morality in Islam
Guidance on worship, character, and daily life
primary_purpose: To compile an authentic and systematically organized collection of the sayings, actions, approvals, and descriptions of the Prophet Muhammad, serving as a primary source for Islamic law, faith, and moral guidance.

structure_format.narrative_style: Scholarly, formal, with isnad (chain of narration) for each hadith
structure_format.organization: Divided into books (kutub) by topics such as faith, purification, prayer, fasting, zakat, pilgrimage, ethics, social matters, and jurisprudence. Each book is further divided into chapters containing specific hadiths.
features: Complete isnad (chain of narrators) preceding every hadith
Classification and grading based on rigor of transmission

key_concepts_lessons: Reliability and transmission of religious teachings through authenticated chains
Comprehensive guidance on all aspects of Islamic practice and belief
Central importance of the Prophet's example in Muslim life
Contextual understanding of faith, ethics, worship, and jurisprudence
Precedent for later Islamic legal, theological, and ethical reasoning
notable_features: Second most authentic collection of hadith in Sunni Islam, after Sahih al-Bukhari
Rigorous methodology for authenticity (sahih) and arrangement
Respected by all major Islamic schools of thought
Frequently cited in legal, theological, and spiritual discourses
cultural_historical_context: Compiled in 9th-century Persia during the Islamic Golden Age, a period marked by heightened attention to collecting, scrutinizing, and preserving the sayings of the Prophet Muhammad. Sahih Muslim emerged as one of the 'Kutub al-Sittah' (six major hadith collections) that shaped Sunni scholarship, law, and society.
reception_impact: Universally regarded among Sunni Muslims as a foundational source of authentic hadith
Essential reference in Islamic jurisprudence, theology, and worship
Studied intensively in seminaries and by lay Muslims worldwide
Translated into many languages and widely available
Subject of numerous commentaries and scholarly works
comparable_titles: Sahih al-Bukhari by Imam Muhammad al-Bukhari
Sunan Abu Dawud by Abu Dawud al-Sijistani
Sunan Ibn Majah by Ibn Majah
